entries.text: Started from a terminal, OverlayLock's help, version and error text now appears before the prompt instead of below it, and the terminal waits for the lock to end, so scripts get its exit code; started from a shortcut or a Stream Deck button, it still opens no console window.

Running `cargo xtask dist` builds OverlayLock for your processor and puts a ready-to-run copy in the `!Distribution` folder, replacing only its own files so the path stays the same for a Stream Deck button or shortcut; `cargo xtask dist --zip <folder>` writes the x64 and ARM64 release zips with their SHA-256 sums instead.
OverlayLock can be downloaded from the GitHub Releases page as a zip for x64 or ARM64 PCs, and a maintainer can publish a new release from the Actions tab with Release > Run workflow.
OverlayLock has its own rainbow lock-screen icon, in the same style as SpectraWrite's.

`overlay-lock --help` opens with the program's name, version and author, and lists every option: block the keyboard or the mouse system-wide, end the lock after a timeout, ignore Alt+F4, cover only the monitor under the cursor, and step back after Ctrl+Alt+Del so Task Manager can be used.

OverlayLock covers every monitor with a plain screen and hides the cursor until you type the password you gave it on the command line, and it can show a centred message in the colours, size and font you choose.
